Optimal.Notes: This profile targets a stable 30 fps with a 40 Hz refresh rate for reduced input latency, balancing visual quality and battery; bumping textures to Medium and view distance to Medium makes the world noticeably more readable without tanking performance. Drop shadows and ground clutter back to Low if frame rate dips in jungle biomes.

profiles.Summary: ARK: Survival Evolved is a demanding open-world survival game that runs on Unreal Engine 4 and pushes the Steam Deck hard; expect low-to-medium settings with FSR upscaling to maintain playable frame rates. The game is Steam Deck Verified and runs via Proton, though it is known to be one of the more CPU/GPU-intensive titles even at minimum PC specs.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 670 / HD 7870, roughly on par with the Deck GPU), ARK's well-known Unreal Engine 4 performance characteristics, and the Deck hardware spec. On your first run, check frame rate in an open outdoor area and inside a built base — if you see sustained dips below 25 fps in the Optimal profile, switch to Max Battery and reduce View Distance further.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a hard 8 W TDP cap keeps the battery alive longest; the -sm4 launch option forces Shader Model 4 which reduces GPU overhead noticeably on this title. Expect occasional dips below 30 in very busy outdoor areas.

KnownIssues: ARK is notoriously unoptimized and can stutter heavily in dense areas or when many dinosaurs are on screen, even at low settings.
Long initial shader compilation and loading times are common on Deck.
VAC-enabled multiplayer servers may have connectivity or anti-cheat compatibility issues under Proton.
The game's UI and text can be very small at 1280x800; font scaling options in settings are recommended.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full 15 W TDP with GPU at max clock gives the best the Deck can realistically offer; a 40 fps cap at 40 Hz keeps frame pacing smooth and prevents the GPU from chasing uncapped frames wastefully. Be aware that dense base areas with many structures and tamed dinos can still cause dips to the high 20s regardless of settings due to ARK's CPU-side bottlenecks.

Optimal.Notes: A 30 fps cap with FSR upscaling from 1024x640 keeps the game mostly stable while allowing medium textures and view distance for a more enjoyable survival experience. Drop View Distance to Low if frame rate becomes unstable in busy outdoor areas.

profiles.Summary: ARK: Survival Evolved is a demanding open-world survival game that pushes the Steam Deck hard, requiring low settings and upscaling to maintain playable frame rates. It runs under Proton with gold-tier compatibility, meaning most players get it working well but may encounter occasional issues.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 670/HD 7870, which the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU roughly matches or slightly exceeds), ProtonDB gold-tier status, and ARK's well-known poor optimization on PC. On your first run, check frame rate in an open coastal area and near any player base — those are the hardest scenarios — and step down to Max Battery settings if the Optimal profile stutters.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a low TDP cap gives the longest session life; expect occasional dips below 30 fps near large bases or during creature-heavy events. The -sm4 -d3d10 launch options reduce shader complexity and can meaningfully improve performance on lower-end hardware.

KnownIssues: VAC-enabled multiplayer may cause issues connecting to official servers under Proton; unofficial/non-VAC servers are more reliable
Long initial shader compilation can cause stuttering on first run and after updates
High RAM/VRAM usage in dense areas or large bases can cause frame drops and stuttering
Game is notoriously unoptimized on PC; even low settings can dip below 30 fps in complex scenes on the Deck

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running uncapped TDP at 40 Hz/40 fps via the OLED's variable refresh gives the smoothest possible experience; 40 fps feels very fluid at 40 Hz and is more attainable than 60 fps for this unoptimized engine. Expect drops into the low 30s in heavily built-up areas or during large dino encounters.
